Si racconta che lungo le vie dei mercant: They say that along the merchant routes crossing the Sinai, among spices, incense and fine fabrics, there travelled a flask that no one ever sold. It held the Elisir d’Oriente: not a perfume, but a habit. To pause. To watch the sea at dawn. To make a wish before the sun had fully risen. Those who did, so the story goes, always came back. We never found the flask. But we found the place where the habit makes sense: a balcony above the pool, a few steps from the Red Sea, in the part of the resort that bears its name.
Nell’antico Egitto lo scarabeo era il si: In ancient Egypt, the scarab symbolised Khepri, the rising sun, and renewal. When you arrive, you will find a small scarab in your room, its story on papyrus and a postcard for your wish. At your first dawn, step onto the balcony, hold the scarab up to the light, turn it three times and make a wish. Write your wish on the papyrus and leave it in the Scrigno dell’Elisir: it will be waiting if you return. The scarab is yours to keep. Share the moment with #RisveglioDelloScarabeo and @oasidelfaraone.

Il piccolo rito dell’alba di Elisir d’Or: The little dawn ritual of Elisir d’Oriente at Domina Coral Bay: the tale of the flask, Khepri’s scarab and a wish from the balcony above the pool.
At your first dawn, step out onto the balcony.
Tieni lo scarabeo nel palmo, rivolto ver: Hold the scarab in your palm, facing the light, turn it three times clockwise and silently make a wish.
Scrivi il desiderio su uno dei biglietti: Write your wish on one of the small white cards, fold it and slip it under the room’s guardian statue. There it stays, and no one reads it.
Lo scarabeo è tuo: portalo a casa. Si di: The scarab is yours: take it home. They say that whoever brings it back to the Oasis always finds the room free, and a small gift awaits on your return.
Nell’antico Egitto lo scarabeo era il si: In ancient Egypt the scarab was the symbol of Khepri, the sun that rises every morning: rebirth and new beginnings. It was one of the most popular lucky charms.
È un piccolo gioco raccontato con un sor: It’s a little game told with a smile, not a promise of good fortune. Please don’t collect sand, shells or coral: it is forbidden in Egypt and harms the sea.
